name: Work permits and study-to-work routes: rules in force in late 2026
name_fr: Permis de travail et passage études-travail : règles fin 2026
description: Key current rules for employer-specific (LMIA) work permits, open work permits for spouses, and post-graduation work permits.

attributes.legal_status: in force on the access date

lmia_low_wage_refusal.rule: ESDC does not process low-wage LMIA applications for work locations in census metropolitan areas with an unemployment rate of 6% or higher, unless exempt (e.g. primary agriculture, construction, food manufacturing, hospitals, nursing and residential care, some in-home caregivers, positions of about 120 days or less).
lmia_low_wage_refusal.note: List read from a search extract of the ESDC table; re-check before use.

attributes.spousal_open_work_permit: Spouses of workers not on a PR pathway qualify only if the worker is in TEER 0 or 1 (any occupation) or TEER 2–3 in select occupations, and the worker's permit is valid at least 16 more months when the spouse applies; TEER 4–5 not eligible (rules since 21 January 2025).
attributes.post_graduation_work_permit: Language: CLB/NCLC 7 for bachelor's, master's or doctoral graduates; CLB/NCLC 5 for other programmes (tests under 2 years old). Field of study: non-degree graduates whose study-permit application was made on or after 1 November 2024 must have studied in a listed field linked to long-term shortages; IRCC made no changes to the list for 2026.
attributes.international_mobility_program: LMIA-exempt permits (e.g. trade agreements, intra-company transfers, spousal permits, PGWP) are issued under the International Mobility Program; individual categories not catalogued in this pass.
attributes.status_dependency: Applies according to the user's citizenship, status, occupation, language scores, age and family — all unknown (USER-PROFILE.md 'Facts about the user'; OPEN-QUESTIONS.md items 1, 2, 4, 7).
